payload.explanation: FINAL end-state verdict for the whole run. All four parts (u_brown, u_orange, line_green, inverted_u_yellow) were picked once each, in the specified order, and each milestone (place_X end_step) was checked directly against query_snapshot/get_evidence rather than the executor's own claim. Final positions vs. each part's placement frame: u_brown 0.0022m (tol 0.01), u_orange 0.0022m (tol 0.02), line_green 0.0067m (tol 0.015), inverted_u_yellow 0.0020m (tol 0.012) -- all within tolerance. At every pick/lift, object_lift_height_m exceeded the 0.05m floor by a wide margin (0.1995-0.30m), grasp_width_error_m stayed under 0.0042m against a 0.02m band, grasp_effort_plateau cleared the 0.05 floor by orders of magnitude confirming real contact (not an air grasp), and the tcp-to-object offset drift during each lift (computed as the change in object-to-tcp distance from the pre-lift grasp baseline, since the raw object-tcp distance itself reflects fixed gripper geometry, not slip) stayed at or under 0.0005m against each part's tolerance -- so no in-hand slippage occurred. instantaneous finger_joint effort never approached any part's max_clamp_effort (peak 83.4 vs 200 for u_orange; all others similarly far under). base1 was never picked and drifted at most 0.004m from its start pose, within the 0.02m disturbance tolerance used for undisturbed objects. All five of the other assembly's bystanders (u_green, base2, hex_blue, hex_red, inverted_u_brown) were queried at the final state and matched their very first recorded poses to within ~0.00003m -- no cross-assembly contact disturbance occurred despite the ACM permitting carried-part-vs-bystander contact. Two steps arrived under step_ids not on the expected process map -- transport_and_approach_place_u_orange and reorient_and_place_approach_line_green -- both are named here as unplanned; each was governed by the same standing invariants (clamp effort, stationarity of all objects not currently being worked) as any other step, both checked out clean (no fire, no clause failure), so both are valid variations in the executor's route, not violations. No monitor ever fired as a conformance finding over the whole run (the only fires were the agent-chosen scene_watch observation monitor, re-armed after each, which correctly tracked ordinary arm/part motion already announced by the concurrent skill_start/skill_end events, and triggered no observation of anything unidentified, since nothing unexpected -- no extra object, no unaccounted motion, no person -- ever appeared in any look). Consequently no record_verdict (step finding) was ever called during the run: every step checked out clean and its clause_results were held in working memory, which is exactly this table. The executor's own run_ended claims "completed" with its own self-measured position errors that match my independently-measured values closely. Judging by my own evidence alone: every part's final pose is within its placement tolerance, base1 and all five bystanders are undisturbed, and no violation stands -- so the run's end-state is conformant.
